study_identification.author_journal_year: Di Biase et al., Molecular Psychiatry, 2022
study_identification.title: Cell type-speciﬁc manifestations of cortical thickness heterogeneity in schizophrenia

study_characteristics.study_objective: The study aims to determine if cortical thickness (CTh) heterogeneity in schizophrenia is related to interregional variation in different neural cell types. This is investigated by combining normative modeling of CTh with gene expression data and validating the findings with person-specific genomic data.

dataset_name.answer: HCP-Young Adult Sample; HCP for Early Psychosis (HCP-psychosis)

hc_sex.answer: HCP-1200: 575 (54%) F; HCP-Psychosis: 23 (37%) F. Combined: 598 (53%) F

quality_checking_detail.answer: For the HCP-psychosis cohort, raw data were checked for anatomical, processing and noise issues. FreeSurfer quality control was performed as per ENIGMA protocols. For the HCP-1200 cohort, subjects with documented brain anatomical, processing or noise issues (n=151) based on the HCP supplied 'QC_Issue' variable were excluded.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: ComBat harmonization was used to alleviate possible site-related differences, while retaining biological variation related to diagnosis, sex and age. For HCP (discovery), each measure was harmonized across 4 sites: HCP-young adult sample (site 1) and 3 sites comprising the HCP-Psychosis dataset.

predictor_effects.answer: The model is `CTh𝑖(𝜏) = 𝛽0(𝜏) + 𝛽1(𝜏)sex𝑖 + 𝛽2(𝜏)(age𝑖 − 𝐴) + 𝛽3(𝜏)sex𝑖(age𝑖 − 𝐴) + 𝛽4(𝜏)(age𝑖 − 𝐴)2`. It doesn't explicitly state fixed or random effects, but given the model, they are treated as fixed effects.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study uses ComBat for site effect harmonization and includes age and sex as covariates in the normative model, addressing nuisance variables.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: Regional CTh estimates were retrospectively harmonized with ComBat [7] to alleviate possible site-related differences, while retaining biological variation related to diagnosis, sex and age. and Quantile regression [18] was used to obtain a normative range of regional CTh variation as a function of age and sex [3] (see Supplementary Material for model details).

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The normative model's accuracy is confirmed by showing that over 90% of the healthy individuals (the training set) reside within the established normative range.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: For all cortical regions, more than 90% of the healthy individuals resided within the normative range, conﬁrming the accuracy of the normative models.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The study does not appear to use a separate independent dataset from the same domain for validation of the normative model itself. The ASRB cohort is used for clinical validation, but not for validating the normative model's performance on unseen healthy controls from the same data distribution as the training set.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The study uses the ASRB dataset as a validation cohort, which is from a different domain (different scanners, age range, etc.) to validate the overall findings and the clinical application of the normative model.
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: The ASRB dataset was used to evaluate replicability and validity (n = 520 comprising 335 cases [age: 39.70 ± 10.81; 100(30%) females] and 185 controls [age: 41.05 ± 14.02); 94(51%) females]).

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: The study uses several analyses. It correlates interregional levels of cell type-specific gene expression with individual deviations in regional CTh estimates. It uses the Ansari-Bradley test to see if the correlation distributions are more dispersed than a null distribution. It uses Ward's linkage clustering to identify patient subtypes. Finally, it uses partial correlations to assess the degree to which polygenic cell type scores covary with severity in whole-brain CTh deviations in individuals comprising the corresponding subtype.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: CTh heterogeneity in schizophrenia relates to inter-individual variation in cell-type specific functions, allowing for the stratification of patients into biologically meaningful subtypes.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: The study found that CTh deviations in schizophrenia were associated with the gene expression of five neural cell types. This allowed for the clustering of patients into three subtypes. In a neuronal/endothelial subtype, CTh deviations covaried with polygenic risk from neuronal and endothelial cell genes (r = -0.40, p = 0.010). In a glia/OPC subtype, CTh deviations covaried with polygenic risk from glia and OPC-linked genes (r = -0.30, p = 0.028).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The use of gene expression data from healthy adult donors cannot precisely capture interregional expression patterns in individuals with schizophrenia. The patterns of CTh alterations that do not map neatly onto specific cell types may weaken the predictive power of polygenic risk. The estimation of cell type transcriptional maps is dependent on the source data used to extrapolate gene sets.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The study proposes a novel method to stratify schizophrenia patients into biologically meaningful subtypes using a multi-scale approach, which could guide future research and in vitro disease models.
